items.title: Canonical LSI to finite KL--Fisher bridge

source.anchor: Definition 1.2.25 and the standard canonical-density specialization
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi; ASTIS supplies the RN/KL and generator-domain formal details. No author endorsement implied.

items.statement: An established density-form generator LSI, applied to the admissible canonical RN density and combined with the canonical Dirichlet--Fisher identity, gives finite Mathlib KL and KL ≤ (C/2) FI.
assumptions: Canonical density entropy is integrable and normalized.
The canonical score is genuinely differentiable almost everywhere with integrable squared norm.
Generator integration-by-parts, symmetry and carré-du-champ/score identities hold for this pair.
For the Lee--Shen--Tian curvature rate lambda, substitute C=lambda^{-1}.

formulae.label: finite canonical KL and Fisher control

obligations.label: Apply generator LSI to the canonical density without losing entropy finiteness or score domains

bindings.boundary: Conditional canonical bridge only; no Gibbs LSI, Bakry--Emery, T2 or W2 result.

assumption_deltas.source: Paper prose applies LSI to a density ratio.
assumption_deltas.lean: Nonnegativity, normalization, entropy and generator-energy integrability are explicit in LogSobolevAdmissible.
assumption_deltas.reason: They make the entropy and Dirichlet expressions genuine finite integrals.

assumption_deltas.source: SALD/LST write a positive rate c_LSI or lambda.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source specialization must state C=1/c_LSI or C=1/lambda.

assumption_deltas.source: The restricted-Gaussian argument also invokes strong convexity and Talagrand T2.
assumption_deltas.reason: Concrete strong-convex Gibbs LSI and T2 remain independent analytic red nodes.
